rationales: Metallic bonding occurs between metal atoms, not because the electronegativity difference is below 1.7.
An ionic bond is generally associated with a large electronegativity difference.
A difference below 1.7 generally indicates a covalent bond.
Coordinate covalent bonding involves a shared pair donated by one atom, which is not specified by this difference alone.
Each oxygen atom shares two pairs of electrons, forming a double covalent bond.
A single bond shares only one pair of electrons.
A triple bond shares three pairs of electrons and is not present in O₂.
O₂ is made of nonmetals sharing electrons, not transferring them.
Graphite is a soft form of carbon, not an extremely hard one.
Iodine is a relatively soft molecular solid.
Diamond is an extremely hard form of carbon.
Phosphorus is not an extremely hard nonmetal.
9.8 g is one-tenth of the mass of a mole of H₂SO₄.
98 amu is the molecular mass expressed in atomic mass units, not the molar mass.
H₂SO₄ has a molar mass of 98 g in the textbook convention (98 g/mol).
9.8 amu is neither its molecular mass nor its molar mass.
An s-subshell has one orbital.
A p-subshell does not have two orbitals.
A p-subshell contains three orbitals.
A d-subshell, not a p-subshell, has five orbitals; no subshell has four orbitals.
The second and third periods are called short periods.
Long periods refer to periods with more elements, such as the fourth and fifth.
Normal periods is not the name for the second and third periods.
Very long periods are the sixth and seventh periods.
There are more than two bond links in H–C≡C–H.
Counting the triple bond as three, the molecule has five bonds, not three.
The two C–H bonds plus the C≡C triple bond give five bond links, not four.
H–C≡C–H has two single bonds and one triple bond, making five covalent bonds.
N₂ is nonpolar, so this pair does not consist of two molecules with polar covalent bonds.
Both O₂ and Cl₂ are nonpolar molecules.
H₂O is polar, but C₂H₂ is nonpolar overall.
Both H₂O and HCl have polar covalent bonds.
Percent volume by volume uses the volumes of both solute and solution.
Mass of solute divided by mass of solution, multiplied by 100, is percent m/m.
Percent mass by volume uses solute mass and solution volume.
Percent volume by mass uses solute volume and solution mass.
Sugar dissolves readily in water.
Alcohol mixes with water.
Glucose dissolves in water.
Benzene is nonpolar and does not dissolve in water.
Avogadro’s number is not 6.02 × 10²⁴ particles.
Avogadro’s number is not a negative power of ten.
Avogadro’s number is approximately 6.02 × 10²³ particles.
6.02 × 10²⁰ is too small to be Avogadro’s number.
The sixth period contains more than two elements.
The sixth period contains more than eight elements.
The sixth period includes the lanthanides and has 32 elements in total.
The sixth period has 32 elements.
The K shell has one subshell.
The N shell has four subshells: s, p, d, and f.
The L shell has two subshells.
The O shell has five subshells.
CO₂ has three atoms and is a polyatomic molecule.
HCl has only two atoms and is diatomic, not polyatomic.
H₂O has three atoms and is a polyatomic molecule.
CH₄ has five atoms and is a polyatomic molecule.
H₂O has a bent shape and is polar.
Cl₂ consists of identical atoms and is nonpolar.
HCl has a polar bond and is a polar molecule.
HF has a polar bond and is a polar molecule.
